title: Introduce eval-debiasing-oracle and gradient-stability CI adapter
author: Marta Kline
release_notes:
- Add 'eval-debiasing-oracle' metric shim that computes per-cohort debiased scores and exposes a normalized delta for CI gating.
- Add 'gradient-stability-adapter' CI hook that tracks metric gradient variance between baseline and candidate and escalates regressions when instability exceeds thresholds.
- New smoke-eval profile 'debiased-smoke' for faster pre-merge checks.
- Docs: evaluation/ oracles and ci adapters documentation and config examples.
description: Context: As part of efforts to detect subtle quality regressions we observed in prompt cohorts that correlate with demographic and style axes, we need both a stable debiasing-aware signal and a way to flag sharp metric gradient changes that precede behavioral regressions. This PR introduces two coordinated pieces: (1) an eval-debiasing-oracle that computes cohort-aware adjusted scores and returns a single normalized 'debiased_delta' used by CI gates, and (2) a gradient-stability-adapter CI hook that computes per-metric gradient variance across prompt partitions and allows progressive soft-fail -> hard-block policies. Motivation: existing per-prompt SLOs can be noisy for small cohorts; debiasing oracle reduces noise by combining a lightweight reweight + calibration step while preserving sensitivity to meaningful shifts. The gradient-stability adapter helps catch brittle regressions where mean metric change is small but gradient variance increases (indicating divergent failure modes). This is a production-oriented change: added a fast smoke profile to keep CI latency low while preserving signal fidelity for main gates. Changes: - New module eval_harness/oracles/debiasing_oracle.py implementing reweighting, stratified bootstrap calibration, and an exported scoring shim compatible with existing eval orchestration. - New CI hook eval_harness/ci_hooks/gradient_stability_adapter.py that integrates into existing eval CI pipeline. The adapter supports config options: window_size, variance_threshold, soft_fail_ratio, quarantine_ttl. - Integration tests under tests/eval_oracles/test_debiasing_oracle.py and tests/ci_hooks/test_gradient_stability_adapter.py - New smoke profile: config/smoke_profiles/debiased-smoke.yaml - Docs: docs/eval/oracles/debiasing-oracle.md and docs/ci/gradient-stability-adapter.md - Example alert mapping and Linear automation in scripts/ci/linear_autoresponder.py Checklist: - [x] Implementation and unit tests - [x] Smoke profile added to CI matrix - [x] Docs and examples added - [x] Reviewed and addressed feedback from reviewers Risk: low-to-medium; new thresholds are conservative by default and require opt-in via project configuration. Rollout plan: merged behind feature flag in CI config; ops will enable for a subset of repositories for 2 weeks and monitor false positive rate. Related: Linear ENG-2345 (cohort regression guard), ENG-2399 (eval infra observability), SUP-1182 (customer-reported cohort drift).

review_thread: Evan Park: High level: I like the idea of reducing cohort noise, but can you clarify the assumptions of the reweighting? Is there a chance of masking a real regression if cohort sizes change dramatically?

Marta Kline: Reply: Good point — the oracle logs cohort cardinalities and exposes an 'effective_sample_factor' in telemetry; we also abort reweighting when any cohort has < 50 examples and fall back to raw scoring. Added tests for that case.
Lina Chen: Please add a config option to disable bootstrap calibration (I want to test pure reweighting in some baseline runs).
Marta Kline: Added 'calibration.enabled' toggle and updated docs with example toggles. Also added a small benchmark in tests that runs both modes and asserts expected variance reduction.
Diego Morales: CI adapter looks good; one ask — include a lightweight histogram view in telemetry for gradient variance so we can triage which prompts drive the instability.
Marta Kline: Added telemetry histogram export to eval telemetry and a short example Kibana dashboard snippet in docs.
Evan Park: Approving after one nit on doc wording in the README.
